biography:
Phill Scragg is a British jazz musician and long-time collaborator of the renowned English actor and musician Matt Berry. Scragg performs primarily in the jazz genre, often blending instrumental and electronic influences to create a distinctive sound that explores both traditional and experimental territories. He is best known as a core member of the Matt Berry Trio, where he works alongside fellow long-time collaborator Graham Mann to accompany Berry's musical vision.

As a key figure in Berry's ensemble, Scragg contributed significantly to the trio's debut album, Everything's Peachy, released as the second volume of Acid Jazz Records' "Jazz Sessions" series. The album showcases the trio's exploration of jazz, instrumental, and electronic textures, inspired by the sky exploits of The Sun. Scragg's compositional role is evident on the album, where he co-composed tracks alongside Berry and Mann, demonstrating his creative input beyond performance.

Scragg's collaboration with Berry extends beyond the trio, as he also appeared on Berry's eleventh studio album, Heard Noises, released in January 2025. His involvement in this project further highlights his versatility and importance within Berry's musical circle. Through his work in jazz and his enduring partnership with Matt Berry, Phill Scragg has established himself as a significant contributor to the contemporary British jazz and experimental music scene.
